finding.claim: The icon URL supplied to PUT /profile is stored without any validation and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync job, allowing SSRF to internal hosts, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), or arbitrary URLs.
finding.sink: HttpClient.send(HttpRequest GET to URI.create(iconUrl)) in Profile.sync

trace.note: this.iconUrl = icon stored with no validation
sync() builds GET request to URI.create(iconUrl) and sends it with the HttpClient

finding.guards_checked: Only `webhook` is validated (line 12, full-match regex restricting it to https://hooks.example.com/<20 alnum>, so the webhook request at line 21 is not exploitable). `icon` has no scheme, host, or allowlist check, no private/loopback IP blocking, and no redirect restriction is visible on the HttpClient (passed in as parameter).

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the unvalidated `icon` (only `webhook` is regex-checked at line 12) and src/Profile.java:23 sends a GET to URI.create(iconUrl), with no other callers or guards anywhere in the directory.
